title: Restriction after applying noise
statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in\bbr$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$. Write $f_0,f_1$ for its restrictions to the last coordinate, and set $a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$ and $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$. For either bit $b\in\{0,1\}$, the restriction of the noise operator applied to $f$ satisfies
\[
(T_\rho f)_b=T_\rho a_f+\sigma(b)\rho T_\rho d_f,
\]
where $\sigma(0)=1$ and $\sigma(1)=-1$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the Boolean cube of dimension $n+1$ to $\bbr$
replaced: Let $T_\rho$ denote Boolean noise with real correlation $\rho$, whose Fourier multiplier on a set of size $k$ is $\rho^k$. For $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, put $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, $a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$, and $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, and let $s_0=1$, $s_1=-1$. For either bit $b$, $(T_\rho f)_b=T_\rho a_f+s_b\rho T_\rho d_f$ as functions on $\{0,1\}^n$.
